speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're a child experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mouth or gums, and tiny red spots on your skin. To understand what's causing this, have you noticed any bruising on your arms or legs, or does it happen after minor bumps? Have you or your parents ever been told you might have a bleeding disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The clinical presentation of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae, and ecchymoses in a 4-year-old is classic for ITP. I will now request a Complete Blood Count (CBC) with platelet count and a peripheral blood smear to confirm the diagnosis.
